title: Establishing Single-Cell Based Co-Cultures in a Deterministic Manner with a Microfluidic Chip
protocol: Dehydrate a 4-inch silicon wafer in a 120 °C oven for 15 min.
Spin coat 4 g of SU-8 2 negative photoresist onto a 4-inch silicon wafer at 1,000 rpm for 30 s to create a 5 µm thick layer (layer #1).
Soft bake layer #1 on a 65 °C hotplate for 1 min.
Transfer layer #1 to a 95 °C hotplate for 3 min.
Cool layer #1 to room temperature.
Place layer #1 onto the holder of the semi-automatic mask aligner and align with the layer #1 chrome-plated photomask (capture-site layer).
Expose layer #1 with 365 nm UV light at a dose of 150 mJ/cm².
Post-bake layer #1 on a 65 °C hotplate for 1 min.
Transfer layer #1 to a 95 °C hotplate for 1 min.
Cool layer #1 to room temperature.
Immerse layer #1 in a propylene glycol monomethyl ether acetate solution to wash away the uncrosslinked photoresist for 2 min.
Gently dry layer #1 with nitrogen gas to reveal a layer #1 alignment mark.
Cover the layer #1 alignment mark by an adhesive tape.
Spin coat 4 g of SU-8 10 negative photoresist onto the layer #1 at 1,230 rpm for 30 s to create a 25 µm thick layer #2.
Remove the tape.
Soft bake layer #2 on a 65 °C hotplate for 3 min.
Transfer layer #2 to a 95 °C hotplate for 7 min.
Cool layer #2 to room temperature.
Place layer #2 onto the holder of the semi-automatic mask aligner.
Align the layer #2 chrome-plated photomask (bypass channel layer) to the layer #1 alignment mark.
Expose layer #2 with 365 nm UV light at a dose of 200 mJ/cm².
Remove layer #2 from the aligner and post-bake on a 65 °C hotplate for 1 min.
Transfer layer #2 to a 95 °C hotplate for 3 min.
Cool layer #2 to room temperature.
Cover the layer #1 alignment mark by adhesive tape.
Spin coat 4 g of SU-8 2050 negative photoresist onto layer #2 at 1,630 rpm for 30 s to create a 100 µm thick layer #3.
Remove the tape and soft bake layer #3 on a 65 °C hotplate for 5 min.
Transfer layer #3 to a 95 °C hotplate for 20 min.
Cool layer #3 to room temperature.
Place layer #3 onto the holder of the semi-automatic mask aligner.
Align the layer #3 chrome-plated photomask (culture chamber layer) to the layer #1 alignment mark.
Expose layer #3 with 365 nm UV light at a dose of 240 mJ/cm².
Remove layer #3 from the aligner and post-bake on a 65 °C hotplate for 5 min.
Transfer layer #3 to a 95 °C hotplate for 10 min.
Cool layer #3 to room temperature.
Immerse in a propylene glycol monomethyl ether acetate solution to wash away the uncrosslinked photoresist for 10 min.
Gently dry with nitrogen gas.
Place the wafer mold and weighing dish containing 100 µL of trichlorosilane in a desiccator.
Apply a vacuum (-85 kPa) for 15 min.
Stop the vacuum and silanize the wafer mold at 37 °C for at least 1 h.
Mix PDMS base and PDMS curing agent in a ratio of 10:1.
Pour 20 g of mixed PDMS onto the wafer mold in a 15 cm dish.
Place the 15 cm dish into a desiccator and apply vacuum (-85 kPa) for 1.5 min.
Keep the dish at room temperature for 20 min.
Remove residual air bubbles in PDMS with nitrogen gas.
Place the 15 cm dish in an oven at 65 °C for 2-4 h to cure PDMS.
Remove the PDMS replica from the wafer mold.
Punch a 1.5 mm inlet and a 0.5 mm outlet on the PDMS using appropriate punchers.
Clean the PDMS replica and slide surface with removable tape.
Treat the surface with oxygen plasma (100 W for 14 s).
Manually align the PDMS replicas with the slide and bring them into contact.
Place the aligned PDMS slide in a 65 °C oven for 1 day.
Immerse the PDMS device in a container filled with phosphate buffered saline.
Place the PDMS device into a desiccator.
Apply vacuum (-85 kPa) for 15 min to remove air bubbles.
Sterilize the PDMS device with UV light (light wavelength: 254 nm) for 30 min.
Replace the PDMS device buffer with medium (DMEM-F12 basal medium containing 1% antibiotic and 10% fetal bovine serum).
Incubate the PDMS device at 4 °C for 1 day to prevent cells from adhering to the PDMS surface.
Remove the culture medium when the cells achieve 70-80% confluence.
Gently wash the cells with 5 mL of sterile PBS three times.
Add 1 mL of DMEM-F12 medium containing 1 µM fluorescent dye into WNT5B sh4 and pLKO-GFP cells (use MV2 medium for LECs).
Incubate the cells for 30 min at room temperature.
Gently wash the cells with 5 mL of sterile PBS three times.
Remove the PBS and add 2 mL of 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA (0.05% Trypsin-EDTA for LECs).
Incubate the cells for 4 min at room temperature.
Gently tap the tissue culture dish to promote cell detachment.
Add 4 mL of DMEM-F12 medium to disperse WNT5B sh4 and pLKO-GFP cells (For LECs use 3 mL of MV2 medium and 1 mL of trypsin neutralizer solution).
Transfer the cells into a 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 300 x g for 3 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of DMEM-F12 medium gently.
Count the number of live cells in a hemocytometer by using the standard Trypan Blue exclusion method.
Prepare 1 mL of cell suspension at 3 x 10^5 cells/mL concentration in DMEM-F12 medium.
Keep cells on ice to prevent cell aggregation.
Connect a poly-tetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) tube between the outlet of the device and syringe pump.
Remove the medium from the PDMS device.
Add 1 µL of cell suspension at a concentration of 3 x 10^5 cells/mL into the inlet of the PDMS device.
Load the cell suspension into the device by a syringe pump at a flow rate of 0.3 µL/min.
Add 1 µL of DMEM-F12 medium into the inlet of the PDMS device.
Load the DMEM-F12 medium into the device by a syringe pump at a flow rate of 0.3 µL/min.
Flow direction is from the inlet to the outlet.
Load 0.3 µL of DMEM-F12 medium into the device by a syringe pump at a flow rate of 10 µL/min.
Flow direction is from the outlet to the inlet.
Repeat steps for loading other cell types into the device.
Use a microscope with a 4x lens to image each culture chamber after completing the cell capture.
Remove the PTFE tube and seal the inlet and the outlet with polyolefin tape.
Move the PDMS device to a 10 cm culture dish and add 10 mL of sterile PBS around it.
Transfer the culture dish to an incubator set at 37 °C, 5% CO2, and 95% humidity for triple single-cell culture.
Microscopically observe and photograph cell growth every 12 hours.
